A basis label is any map $B:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$; write $A_B(i,l)=A(i,B(l))$, $x_B=A_B^{-1}b$, and $x(B)_j=\sum_{l:B(l)=j}(x_B)_l$, with the total matrix inverse, equal to the zero matrix for a singular square matrix. A point $x\in\mathbb Q^q$ is feasible precisely when $Ax=b$ and all coordinates are nonnegative. The basis is basic feasible precisely when $B$ is injective, $\det A_B\ne0$, and $x_B\ge0$ coordinatewise. The objective is $c^\mathsf Tx$ and the basic objective is $c^\mathsf T x(B)$. For a column $j$ put $d_j=A_B^{-1}A_{\cdot j}$ and $\bar c_j=c_j-\sum_l c_{B(l)}(d_j)_l$; $j$ is improving precisely when it is absent from the image of $B$ and $\bar c_j>0$. A row $l$ may leave for $j$ precisely when $(d_j)_l>0$ and $(x_B)_l/(d_j)_l\le(x_B)_i/(d_j)_i$ for every row $i$ with $(d_j)_i>0$. A pivot from $B$ to $B'$ at $j$ requires $B$ basic feasible and $j$ improving, and requires some such leaving $l$ with $B'$ equal to $B$ with row $l$ replaced by $j$ and $B'$ basic feasible; every ratio-test tie is permitted. An optimal basis here means a basic feasible basis with no improving column, rather than a separately quantified comparison against all feasible objective values. No dimension is assumed positive. The LP is nondegenerate when every basic feasible basis has every coordinate of its basic-value vector strictly positive, and bounded when there is a rational $R$ such that every feasible point $x$ satisfies $|x_j|\le R$ for every column $j$; these universal assertions may be vacuous if there are no such bases or points, and empty dimensions are included. Given a permutation $\omega$ of the $q$ column indices and indices $a,j<q$, define the cyclic distance $\delta_\omega(a,j)=((\omega(j)+q-a)\bmod q)$ using their natural index values and natural subtraction. A Cunningham choice is an improving $j$ with $\delta_\omega(a,j)\le\delta_\omega(a,k)$ for every improving $k$. A Cunningham state consists of a basis label $B$ and an index $a<q$; a step chooses such a $j$, performs the ratio-test pivot just specified, and sets the next stored index equal to $\omega(j)$, not to $j$ unless those indices coincide. A complete Cunningham run of length $T$ is a total sequence of these states with a basic feasible initial basis, a Cunningham step for every natural $t<T$, and an optimal final basis, with no restrictions after $T$. A choice or state requiring an index below $q$ has no instances when $q=0$.

A valuation is any triple $(p_*,P,L)\in\mathbb N\times\mathcal P_{\rm fin}(V)\times\mathbb N$, without intrinsic consistency constraints. The play valuation first takes $p_*$ to be the supremum of the priorities of recurring vertices, with supremum $0$ on the empty set; it classically chooses a recurring vertex $w_*$ of priority $p_*$ if one exists and otherwise uses the starting vertex $v$, takes $L$ to be the least occurrence time of $w_*$ if there is one and $0$ otherwise, and takes $P=\{\pi(k):k<L,\ p_*<p(\pi(k))\}$, as a set of distinct vertices. For any proposed step relation and initial map $\iota$, a complete run of natural length $T$ is a total sequence of maps starting at $\iota$, legal for player $0$ at every $t\le T$, both improvable and taking the proposed step at every $t<T$, and not improvable at $T$; nothing is required after $T$. All these definitions are total; existence, legality, well-formedness, and consistency of valuations are imposed only where explicitly listed, and statements universally ranging over vertices are vacuous when $V$ is empty.
